domain: Duration enrichment: provider estimates, alias rescue, job queue and human reviews
note: The earlier readiness-3 physical gaps are closed by the applied immutable M3 migration: catalog.duration_estimates, catalog.review_decisions, catalog.provider_state and catalog.appid_terminal_rejections exist. Queue lifecycle facts now use those durable relations while raw queue archives remain staging-30d-post-cutover.

game_duration_estimates.role: Per-provider duration estimates with match status, confidence and a jsonb evidence document. The reconcile step chooses between these and writes the winner onto catalog_games.
game_duration_estimates.summary: Per-provider duration evidence is preserved in catalog.duration_estimates keyed (steam_app_id, provider), so a later re-reconcile does not need to re-fetch every provider.

steam_app_id.note: Resolves through migration.game_map to catalog.games.id. Half of the natural (game, provider) key.
steam_app_id.transform: legacy steam appid -> catalog.games.id through migration.game_map. The raw appid is retained as half of the natural key, so an estimate for an app the catalogue does not hold still loads.

provider.note: Which duration provider produced the estimate. Coordinator ruling requires provider to be preserved as a SEPARATE fact from confidence, so it cannot be folded away.

provider_game_id.note: bigint. The provider's own identifier for the matched game - the key that makes an estimate re-checkable, and the anchor for the known HowLongToBeat AppID-identity mismatch on re-released SKUs, where rescue is by exact normalised title or alias rather than by AppID.

main_story_minutes.note: Already EXACT MINUTES; no unit conversion at any point. Would map to a per-provider estimate column, not to catalog.game_features, which holds only the reconciled winner.

main_extra_minutes.note: The middle HowLongToBeat tier. Note the singular 'extra' here versus 'main_extras_minutes' on catalog_games - the two spellings are the same tier and a transform must not treat them as different columns.

submission_count.note: How many provider submissions the estimate aggregates. This is the SAMPLE SIZE and is the only honest basis for the ordinal confidence; discarding it while keeping a confidence label would leave the label unjustifiable.

match_status.note: Whether and how the provider row was matched to the Steam app. Distinguishes a confident match from a title-similarity rescue, which is exactly the distinction the profile_steam AppID mismatch makes necessary.

match_confidence.note: Text ordinal over none|low|medium|high. Same class as readiness 4.5: no defensible numeric image, and inventing one fabricates precision. Preserve as an ordinal label.

provider_updated_at.note: When the PROVIDER last updated the estimate, distinct from checked_at, which is when we looked. Both are needed to decide whether a refresh is due.

checked_at.note: When we last fetched from the provider. NOT NULL in the source.

next_refresh_at.note: Provider refresh schedule preserved in the applied catalog.duration_estimates destination.

last_error_code.note: Why the last fetch failed, as a code rather than free text. Earned history: a persistent provider failure should not be forgotten at cutover.

created_at.note: When the estimate row was first created.

updated_at.note: Row mutation clock; ordinarily a derived-retirement, but unresolved while the relation has no home.

evidence.note: jsonb, NOT NULL. The raw provider response that justifies the estimate. Must be treated as OPAQUE TEXT and hashed as text, never re-serialised (readiness 8.5). Before export it must be checked for anything credential-shaped, since it holds provider responses.

settled_decisions: D-DUR-1 SETTLED: ruling 2 requires duration estimates and provider retry state, and plan 14.2 requires provider evidence and resolver parity. catalog.duration_estimates exists in the M3 migration with a unique (steam_app_id, provider), which is the key this decision asked for.

D-DUR-2 SETTLED: ruling 2 requires ordinal confidence WITHOUT fabricated probabilities. catalog.duration_estimates.match_confidence is a text ordinal constrained to none|low|medium|high, so no numeric image is invented.

game_duration_aliases.role: Operator-authored title aliases that rescue a duration match when AppID identity fails.
game_duration_aliases.summary: Hand-authored provider search aliases are preserved in catalog.duration_aliases as operator decisions a provider refresh must never overwrite.
evidence: coordinator ruling: preserve MANUAL DURATION DECISIONS

steam_app_id.note: Resolves through migration.game_map. The app the alias rescues.
steam_app_id.transform: legacy steam appid -> catalog.games.id through migration.game_map. The alias exists precisely to rescue an app whose identity did not match, so the raw appid is the key and game_id may be NULL.

search_title.note: The exact title to search the provider for. Hand-authored; the entire value of the row. Nonempty text must not be truncated or dropped.

release_year.note: Disambiguates remakes and re-releases sharing a title. An integer YEAR, not a date: it must never be widened into a date or timestamp.

review_status.note: Whether the alias has been reviewed and accepted. An operator DECISION.

notes.note: Operator notes explaining why the alias exists. Empty may normalise to null; nonempty must not be truncated or dropped.

updated_at.note: When it was last edited; for a hand-authored row this is a meaningful edit history, not mere row bookkeeping.

settled_decisions: D-DUR-3 SETTLED: ruling 2 requires aliases and manual duration decisions to be preserved, and plan 14.2 lists aliases explicitly. catalog.duration_aliases is a dedicated relation in the M3 migration, which is the second of the two options this decision offered.

game_duration_jobs.role: Work queue for duration enrichment, with a lock lease and retry state.
game_duration_jobs.summary: Per plan 14.2 and readiness 14 the queue is NOT a migration destination: in-flight work is not resumed and due work is rebuilt. Root's 11 September durability review added the missing half: current lifecycle state for a catalogued app reaches catalog.provider_state (evidence_kind='duration') and a terminal verdict for an uncatalogued app reaches catalog.appid_terminal_rejections, because migration.legacy_duration_job_archive is staging-30d-post-cutover. lib/duration-worker.ts is the sole writer: 'failed' is the verdict after MAX_ATTEMPTS (line 140-143), 'retry' carries the only record of the effective backoff (line 145), and a 'needs_review' row carries a provider verdict such as duration_not_found or known_title_no_provider_times (line 117-127) that re-running cannot change.
game_duration_jobs.target: catalog.provider_state (mapped AppIDs) + catalog.appid_terminal_rejections (terminal verdicts for uncatalogued AppIDs); the transient queue itself is rebuilt after cutover
game_duration_jobs.archive_purpose: Preserve earned failure history so the rebuilt duration queue does not re-attempt known-bad apps against a provider we are rate-limited by, and so a systematic provider outage remains diagnosable after cutover.
game_duration_jobs.archive_retention: Operational provenance with no account key: retained until the v2 duration pipeline has re-derived its own failure set, reviewed at M7.

retention.bound: until the v2 duration pipeline has re-derived its own failure set
authority: docs/VaultShuffle_v2_architecture_plan.md section 13: shared catalogue evidence and job/worker summaries are bounded operational data with no account key

evidence: readiness 14 (queue relations are design confirmations, not migration conflicts)

steam_app_id.note: The app the job was for; kept as the raw appid so an app absent from catalog_games is still recorded.

status.note: Archived verbatim AND mapped to durable lifecycle state; 'retry' becomes 'failed' with its fence, which is the only target shape whose CHECK permits a fence, and a needs_review verdict splits into a terminal rejection (duration_not_found / known_title_no_provider_times) or review_required state.

priority.recoverable_from: Scheduling input for a queue that is rebuilt after cutover from current demand.
priority.note: Retired as scheduling state, not as data.

attempts.note: Earned attempt history; also catalog.appid_terminal_rejections.attempts for an uncatalogued terminal verdict.

next_attempt_at.note: Also catalog.appid_terminal_rejections.retry_allowed_after for a terminal verdict on an AppID with no catalogue row. Reversed from derived-retirement by the 11 September durability review: nothing rebuilds a fence, so retiring it makes every failed app due at once after cutover.

locked_at.recoverable_from: A worker lease with no meaning after the freeze; readiness 14 confirms in-flight work is not resumed.
locked_at.note: A lease held at freeze time is reported to the operator, not carried.

locked_by.recoverable_from: The worker instance holding the lease. Meaningless after cutover, when no v2 worker will recognise the identifier.
locked_by.note: Also the column most likely to carry an environment or host identifier, so it is not exported.

last_error_code.note: The provider verdict code, which is what distinguishes a terminal rejection from a conflict awaiting a human.

last_error_message.note: Kept verbatim within the durable 2000-character bound; an over-long value fails closed rather than being truncated.

created_at.note: When the job was queued; gives the failure history an age.

updated_at.note: Also catalog.appid_terminal_rejections.last_attempt_at. The job row has no completed/processed instant, so updated_at is the only record of when the last attempt was made.

catalog_duration_reviews.role: Human review responses on catalogue durations, optionally attributed to a reviewing user.
catalog_duration_reviews.summary: Operator duration reviews are preserved in catalog.review_decisions with decision_kind 'duration'. A review by a since-deleted account keeps a NULL reviewer rather than being dropped.
evidence: coordinator ruling on manual duration decisions

steam_appid.note: Resolves through migration.game_map. The app reviewed.
steam_appid.transform: legacy steam appid -> catalog.games.id through migration.game_map.

response_text.note: NOT NULL. The review itself. Nonempty text must not be truncated or dropped; empty may normalise to null.

response_kind.note: What kind of response it is (correction, confirmation, rejection). The machine-readable half of the decision.

source_url.note: Where the reviewer got their figure. The evidence behind the decision. Checked for embedded credentials before export.

reviewer_user_id.note: Nullable uuid; resolve through migration.account_map to the nullable reviewer_account_id foreign key. A review by a since-deleted account keeps a null reviewer rather than being dropped.
reviewer_user_id.transform: legacy uuid -> integer account id through migration.account_map. The shared catalogue decision intentionally keeps only the nullable account FK; the source reviewer UUID is available during bounded migration staging and is not retained in this shared row, so ON DELETE SET NULL removes account-linked personal identity while preserving the decision itself.

reviewed_at.note: When the review was made; the ordering key when several reviews disagree.

updated_at.note: When the review was last edited. For a hand-authored decision this is meaningful edit history, not mere row bookkeeping.

settled_decisions: D-DUR-4 SETTLED: ruling 2 requires review/manual-decision destinations and plan 14.2 requires review provenance. catalog.review_decisions.reviewer_account_id is a nullable FK with ON DELETE SET NULL. The source reviewer UUID is bounded staging evidence, so the shared decision outlives the reviewer without leaving personal identity in the catalogue row.
